Python 3 official documentation (docs.python.org/3/library/sqlite3.html, fetched 2026-10-02): SQLite is a lightweight disk-based database that does not require a separate server process; sqlite3 is a standard-library module (documented as optional in some CPython distributions) that opens local database files directly.

alternatives.name: SQLite via stdlib sqlite3
alternatives.description: Store all notes in a single SQLite database file managed through Python's built-in sqlite3 module.
advantages: Transactional, atomic writes protect notes from corruption on crash or partial write (SQLite journaling).
Supports indexed queries, sorting, and full-text search (FTS5) as the note collection grows.
Ships in the Python standard library, so it adds no new dependency and requires no server or network.
One well-defined database file (for example notes.db) simplifies backup and migration.
disadvantages: Data lives in a binary database file, not directly readable or editable with a plain text editor.
Requires writing and maintaining SQL schema and query code.
The bundled SQLite engine differs per CPython build, so advanced features such as FTS5 may vary by environment.
assumptions: The sqlite3 module is present in the CPython builds used to run notes-cli (the official docs mark it as an optional module in some distributions).
The note collection may grow enough that indexed queries and search matter.

alternatives.name: Single JSON file
alternatives.description: Keep all notes as a list of objects in one JSON file, read and written with Python's built-in json module.
advantages: Minimal code: load the file, mutate the list, dump it back; no schema or SQL to maintain.
Human-readable structured text that is easy to inspect, hand-edit, and back up.
Uses only the standard library, adding no dependency and no network access.
disadvantages: Every change rewrites the whole file; an interrupted write can corrupt the entire store unless atomic write-then-rename logic is implemented by hand.
All notes are parsed into memory on each run, so performance degrades as the collection grows.
No built-in indexing or search beyond loading everything and filtering in Python.
Simultaneous writers would conflict, although this project is single-process by design.
assumptions: The note volume stays modest enough for a full in-memory load on every command.
The CLI can implement its own atomic-write handling if durability matters.

alternatives.name: One Markdown file per note
alternatives.description: Store each note as its own Markdown text file inside a notes directory, using the standard library's pathlib for file operations.
advantages: Maximum human readability and editability; notes work directly with editors, grep, git, and file sync tools.
A corrupted or deleted file damages only that note, not the whole collection.
No dependency and no network access; the format is future-proof and tool-agnostic.
disadvantages: Listing, searching, and sorting require directory scans and per-file parsing on every run.
Metadata such as timestamps and tags must live in a front-matter convention the CLI itself defines and parses.
Filesystem limits on filename length and reserved characters constrain note titles and identifiers.
assumptions: Users value direct access to note files as plain text.
Directory scans are acceptable at the expected note volume.

criteria.name: Implementation simplicity for core CRUD
rubric: Large amount of storage machinery to write and maintain for basic add/list/find/delete
Moderate overhead: some schema or convention code to maintain
Small amount of straightforward code with few moving parts

criteria.name: Data integrity and crash safety
rubric: An interrupted write can corrupt or lose the whole store unless extra safety code is added
Damage is contained to individual notes but write safety must be hand-implemented
Atomic, durable, transactional writes are provided by the storage layer itself

criteria.name: Search and scaling as the note collection grows
rubric: Whole store scanned and parsed on every operation; degrades with volume
Per-file directory scans on each operation; workable at moderate volume
Indexed queries and full-text search supported natively by the storage layer

criteria.name: Human readability and tool portability of the data
rubric: Opaque binary format readable only through the CLI
Plain-text notes directly usable with editors, grep, and git

criteria.name: Dependency footprint
rubric: Requires adding a third-party package or external service
Uses only the Python standard library and local files

hard_constraints.description: Must run entirely offline on the user's own machine with no network access (explicit mandatory statement in README.md).
